ctas.label: Check if Load-Shift Bracing suits my knee

intro: In most Indian knees with OA, the damage is on the inner side. Every step presses bone onto that worn spot, and that pressure is where much of the pain comes from. A knee cap only wraps the joint. A Load-Shift brace pushes gently on the knee to shift that weight to the healthier outer side. Less load on the worn side means less pain where it hurts most. Your doctor decides if it's right for you; our team fits it and checks it works.

whatIs.title: What's happening inside an OA knee
paragraphs: Osteoarthritis slowly thins the smooth cartilage that cushions the ends of your bones. As it wears, the knee becomes painful, stiff and sometimes swollen.

In most people it starts on the inner (medial) side of the knee. Years of squatting, sitting cross-legged and standing put extra load there. Over time, the leg can start to bow outward, which pushes even more weight onto that same worn side.
OA doesn't reverse. But the load on the worn side can be changed — and that is what Load-Shift Bracing does.

symptoms.title: Signs your knee may have OA
items: Pain that gets worse with walking, stairs or getting up from a chair
Stiffness in the morning that eases within about 30 minutes
Swelling or warmth after activity
A grinding or crackling feeling when you bend the knee
The knee won't fully straighten or bend
The knee feels like it may give way
Legs slowly becoming bow-shaped

causes.title: Why it happens
items: Age — most common after 50, though more people in their late 30s and 40s are seeing it.
Body weight — every extra kilo adds several kilos of load on the knee with each step.
Old knee injuries — ACL, meniscus or fracture.
Daily posture — squatting, kneeling, long hours standing.
Family history.
Women after menopause.
Bow legs — they load the inner side even more.

treatment.title: How the brace moves the load
steps: A firm push on the knee. A rigid hinge on one side and the straps press gently on the knee, nudging it into slightly better alignment as you walk.
Weight moves to the healthier side. That nudge shifts load away from the worn inner side, where most of the pain starts.
You set the amount. A thumbwheel dial on the hinge adjusts how much load is shifted — no tools. Our team sets it at fitting; you fine-tune as you get used to it.
Warm, slim and wearable. The single hinge sits on one side only, so the brace fits under trousers. The wrap adds warmth and helps with swelling.
treatment.closing:
Proof: braces that shift load in the main knee joint are strongly recommended in the 2019 American College of Rheumatology osteoarthritis guideline.

Where Load-Shift Bracing fits in your treatment

The best results come from combining steps, not choosing one. Your doctor will build the plan.

  1. Exercise and physiotherapy — strengthening the thigh and hip muscles. A brace makes it easier to keep walking and exercising.
  2. Weight management — even a few kilos less reduces load on the knee.
  3. Load-Shift Bracing — for daily walking, work and activity.
  4. Pain medicines and creams — help with symptoms, under your doctor's guidance.
  5. Injections — steroid or hyaluronic acid, in selected patients.
  6. Surgery — for advanced OA, when other steps aren't enough. For many patients, bracing helps them stay comfortable for longer before they need to decide.

Who Load-Shift Bracing suits

Good fit:

  • OA mainly on one side of the knee (usually the inner side)
  • Mild to moderate OA — often described as grade 2 or 3 on X-ray
  • You want to keep walking, working and doing daily tasks

Talk to your doctor first if:

  • OA affects the whole knee badly (end-stage)
  • Your pain is mainly at the front of the knee, around the kneecap
  • You have poor circulation or skin problems around the knee

faq.question: How is this different from a knee cap?
faq.answer: A knee cap (sleeve) gives warmth and a feeling of support. It doesn't change where the weight goes. A Load-Shift brace has a rigid hinge that moves load off the worn side. Different job, different result.

faq.question: Will it cure my OA?
faq.answer: No. Nothing reverses cartilage loss. A Load-Shift brace aims to reduce pain and make walking easier while you follow your doctor's plan.

faq.question: Can it help me avoid knee replacement?
faq.answer: Some patients with mild to moderate OA stay comfortable for years with bracing, exercise and weight management. Advanced OA may still need surgery. Your orthopaedic surgeon is the right person to judge your stage.

faq.question: When do I wear it?
faq.answer: When you're on your feet — walking, working, light exercise. Take it off when sitting or lying down.

faq.question: Can I exercise in it?
faq.answer: Yes — walking, cycling and gentle strength work. Ask your doctor before any high-impact sport.

faq.question: Will it show under clothes?
faq.answer: The hinge sits on one side and is slim, so it usually fits under trousers.

faq.question: Is OA the same as rheumatoid arthritis?
faq.answer: No. OA is wear of the cartilage. Rheumatoid arthritis is the immune system attacking the joints and needs treatment from a rheumatologist.

faq.question: What exercises help?
faq.answer: Thigh and hip strengthening, swimming, stationary cycling and tai chi. Avoid deep squats and long kneeling. A physiotherapist can plan this for your stage.
